regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8% YoY; PMI 54.6","signal_text":"India GDP at 7.8% YoY looks strong until you set it against IIP at 6.7% YoY — down from 8.8% — and core sector at 5.4% YoY, itself decelerating from 6.0%. PMI composite at 54.6 (83rd percentile) is the headline; the tell is that manufacturing PMI slipped to 52.8 while services carried the composite. The inversion: capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity is accelerating, which should be bullish for private capex — but if credit funding tightens as the CD ratio signals, the investment cycle stalls before it matures.","badge_label":"Slowing Pace","badge_type":"b-slow"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 4.45% YoY; Fuel 22.93% YoY","signal_text":"Headline CPI at 4.45% YoY understates the problem: fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY — a 10-year high at the 95th percentile — is feeding into WPI at 9.92% YoY, and WPI leads CPI core with a 2-quarter lag. Core CPI at 3.9% YoY appears contained, but the RBI has already revised its own inflation forecast up to 5.1% YoY from 4.6% — a 50bps revision that the repo rate at 5.25% p.a. does not yet reflect. The second-order effect: if fuel inflation persists at Brent $104/bbl, the real rate turns negative before the RBI acts, eroding the credibility of the pause.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 17.1% YoY; CD ratio 81.4%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 17.1% YoY against deposit growth at 10.8% YoY is a 630bps divergence that the CD ratio at 81.4% credit ÷ deposits (75th percentile historically) only partially captures. NBFC credit growth accelerating to 14.9% YoY from 10.6% signals wholesale funding pressure building in the shadow system. Corporate bond issuance at ₹18,700 cr / month — the lowest decile in a decade — confirms capital markets are not providing the release valve. The last time the CD ratio sustained above 80% with credit growing this fast, macro-prudential tightening via risk weights followed within two quarters.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25% p.a.","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% p.a. is unchanged, but the RBI's own inflation forecast revision to 5.1% YoY makes the real rate calculus uncomfortable: at current CPI of 4.45% YoY, the real rate is 80bps — thin cover for an economy with fuel inflation at the 95th percentile. The RBI is simultaneously managing INR at 97.09 (94th percentile depreciation) and resisting rate hikes that would slow a capex cycle it has spent two years nurturing. That is not a neutral stance — it is a bet that fuel inflation is transitory, and Brent at $104/bbl is not cooperating.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.1% YoY; CU 77.4% of capacity","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY and capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity — up from 75.6% — are the two cleanest signals that the investment cycle is real, not budgetary. The soft spot is core sector at 5.4% YoY, decelerating from 6.0%, but core sector lags capex by one to two quarters, so this is a trailing indicator, not a leading warning. The inversion: private capex accelerates when funding is available and cheap; with CD ratio at 81.4% and corporate bond issuance at a decade low, the credit channel that should finance this cycle is narrowing precisely as order books fill.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST ₹199853 cr/mo; PV 16% YoY","signal_text":"GST at ₹1,99,853 cr / month — up sharply from ₹1,74,116 cr — looks like a demand surge, but the jump deserves decomposition: how much is genuine volume growth versus advance filings or formalization reclassifying informal spend? Passenger vehicle sales at 16% YoY and two-wheeler at 19.7% YoY confirm broad-based demand, with two-wheelers — the rural and semi-urban proxy — outpacing PVs. The divergence to watch: e-commerce GMV at 18% YoY (26th percentile) suggests urban discretionary is not as strong as auto sales imply, and airline passengers at 86.4 mn / month sit at only the 35th percentile.","badge_label":"Demand Surge","badge_type":"b-exp"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 17.1% YoY (latest) vs deposit growth at 10.8% YoY creates a 350 bps divergence. CD ratio at 81.4% credit ÷ deposits (down from 82.5% prior month) remains elevated at 75th percentile historically. Credit-to-deposit gap has widened for 3 consecutive months. NBFC credit growth accelerating at 14.9% YoY (up from 10.6% YoY prior) signals wholesale funding pressure. Corporate bond issuance at 18,700 ₹ cr / month (lowest decile, 0% percentile) indicates capital markets are not absorbing the overflow.","implication":"Overweight private banks with CASA ratios > 45% — they will poach deposits from smaller lenders. Avoid NBFCs with wholesale funding > 30% of liabilities; liquidity stress will force asset sales or margin compression. RBI will likely ease liquidity via OMOs or CRR cuts within 6-8 weeks if deposit growth doesn't accelerate. Position for a 25-50 bps rate cut by Q3 FY27.","pct_10y":75,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 75th percentile has historically preceded either deposit acceleration or RBI policy easing. Last time CD ratio was this tight (2022), RBI cut rates 250 bps over 12 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capex Cycle Firing on All Cylinders","data_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY (latest) signals robust investment demand. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (up from 75.6% prior month, 74th percentile) — two consecutive months of acceleration. Core sector growth at 5.4% YoY (down from 6% prior) is the only soft spot, but this lags capex by 1-2 quarters. PMI composite at 54.6 index (83rd percentile, highest in 10 years) confirms broad-based manufacturing momentum. Order books are filling; lead times extending.","implication":"Overweight capital goods, industrial machinery, and cement stocks. Capex-linked consumption (steel, power, logistics) will drive earnings growth through FY27. Expect 12-15% earnings growth for Nifty50 capex-exposed names. Avoid defensive sectors; rotation into cyclicals is justified. Infrastructure plays (toll roads, ports, power) will see volume acceleration.","pct_10y":74,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 77.4% is mid-cycle; historically, capex accelerates most aggressively when CU moves from 75% to 80%. This cycle is in early innings.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"Retail Equity Inflows Hit Record Highs","data_text":"SIP inflows at 32,297 ₹ cr / month (latest, up from 31,961 ₹ cr / month prior month, 92nd percentile) — rising 2 consecutive months. SIP accounts at 100.18 mn (up from 99.06 mn, 82nd percentile). SIP AUM at 18.62 ₹ lakh cr (up from 18.21 ₹ lakh cr, 93rd percentile) — rising 2 consecutive months. MF AUM at 87.08 ₹ lakh cr (86th percentile, rising 2 consecutive months). DII equity net flows at 58,502 ₹ cr net / month (100th percentile, rising 2 consecutive months). FII equity net at 29,631 ₹ cr net / month (83rd percentile, up from -3,111.9 ₹ cr net / month prior).","implication":"Retail equity participation is at all-time highs. This is late-cycle behaviour — average SIP ticket size is rising (SIP AUM +2.3% vs SIP accounts +1.1%), indicating affluent money entering, not mass retail. Expect volatility to increase; retail will panic-sell on 10-15% correction. Hedge with long-dated puts on Nifty50. Overweight quality large-caps with pricing power; avoid micro-caps and illiquid mid-caps.","pct_10y":92,"pct_note":"SIP inflows at 92nd percentile preceded the 2021 correction by 4-6 months. Current momentum is unsustainable; reversion risk is material.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation Spike Threatens RBI Credibility","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (latest, up from 20.05% YoY prior month, 95th percentile) — highest in 10 years. WPI at 9.92% YoY (up from 9.78% YoY, 67th percentile). Brent crude at 104.43 $/bbl (flat, 73rd percentile). Natural gas at 3.204 $/MMBtu (flat, 20th percentile). Headline CPI at 4.45% YoY (up from 4.38% YoY, 41st percentile) — rising 2 consecutive months. RBI inflation forecast revised up to 5.1% YoY (from 4.6% YoY prior, 53rd percentile).","implication":"Fuel inflation is a policy headwind. If Brent stays above 100 $/bbl for 2+ more months, RBI will be forced to hold rates despite deposit stress. This creates a policy bind: cut rates and risk rupee weakness, or hold and risk credit stress. Expect RBI to communicate a 'data-dependent' pause through Q2 FY27. Overweight energy stocks (ONGC, Reliance) as a hedge; underweight rate-sensitive sectors (NBFCs, housing finance). Monitor geopolitical risk; any Middle East escalation could push Brent to 110-115 $/bbl.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile has historically forced RBI to pause or hike, even when growth is slowing. Last time (2022), RBI hiked 250 bps despite slowing growth.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.5: {"signal_num":5,"signal_theme":"GLOBAL LIQUIDITY","status":"risk","title":"Fed Tightening Bias Resurfaces, Carry Unwinds","data_text":"Fed funds rate at 3.75% p.a. (up from 3.63% p.a., 68th percentile) — rising 2 consecutive months. US 10Y Treasury yield at 5.22% (down from 5.28%, but 95th percentile historically). US core CPI at 2.45% YoY (down from 2.47%, falling 2 consecutive months, 47th percentile). BOJ rate at 1.0% p.a. (up from 0.75% p.a., 86th percentile) — strong-negative signal. ECB deposit rate at 2.25% p.a. (up from 2.0% p.a., 59th percentile). US PMI composite at 56 index (84th percentile, up from 54.5). DXY at 102.231 index (flat, 56th percentile).","implication":"Fed is signalling a higher-for-longer stance; carry trades are unwinding. INR weakness (97.09 ₹/USD, 94th percentile, up 4 of last 5 months) is a direct consequence. BOJ's rate hike to 1.0% p.a. is a major shift — yen carry trades will unwind, creating volatility in emerging markets. Reduce leverage; hedge FX exposure. Expect INR to test 98-99 ₹/USD if Fed holds rates through Q2. Overweight USD-earning exporters; underweight import-heavy sectors.","pct_10y":86,"pct_note":"BOJ at 86th percentile (highest in 10 years) signals a regime shift. Last time BOJ hiked (2023), EM currencies fell 5-8% within 3 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.6: {"signal_num":6,"signal_theme":"INR / FX RESERVES","status":"risk","title":"Rupee Weakness Accelerates, RBI Intervention Likely","data_text":"INR at 97.09 ₹/USD (up from 96.78 ₹/USD, 94th percentile) — rising 4 of last 5 months. Recent sequence: 96.15 → 95.24 → 96.15 → 97.09 (accelerating depreciation). FII equity net at 29,631 ₹ cr net / month (83rd percentile, but volatile: -3,111.9 prior month). DXY at 102.231 index (flat, 56th percentile). US 10Y Treasury at 5.22% yield (95th percentile) — carry trade unwind is underway. India's current account deficit is widening (oil imports rising, exports slowing).","implication":"RBI will likely intervene to defend 97.50 ₹/USD level; expect spot intervention and forward guidance. Expect RBI to sell USD reserves if INR breaches 97.50 ₹/USD. This will tighten liquidity and support rates, conflicting with deposit stress signals. Hedge INR exposure; avoid long USD positions. Exporters should book forward contracts above 97.50 ₹/USD. Importers will face margin pressure; pass-through will be limited.","pct_10y":94,"pct_note":"INR at 94th percentile weakness has historically triggered RBI intervention within 2-3 weeks. Last time (2022), RBI sold ~$20 bn to defend 80 ₹/USD.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Absorption Collapse Signals GCC Pivot","data_text":"Office absorption at 13.2 mn sq ft / quarter (latest, down from 13.7 mn sq ft / quarter, 6th percentile — lowest in 10 years). Recent sequence: 5.2 → 13.2 → 21 → 13.2 → 21 → 13.2 (volatile, but trending down). Office vacancy at 14.5% vacant (down from 15.1%, 42nd percentile). Retail mall vacancy at 4.8% vacant (down from 5.0%, 7th percentile, strong-positive signal). Nifty IT index flat YTD despite Nifty50 +15%. REIT valuations: Embassy at 369.92 ₹/unit (down 14% from 431.27 ₹/unit), Mindspace at 345.06 ₹/unit (down 30% from 490.99 ₹/unit). Home loan disbursements at 19,930 ₹ cr / quarter (up from 15,914 ₹ cr / quarter, but data is sparse). Airline passenger traffic at 86.4 mn / month (up from 85.17 mn / month, but 35th percentile — weak).","implication":"Traditional IT services are NOT the office buyer anymore. Global Capability Centers (GCCs) — captive R&D and engineering hubs of multinational corporates — are the marginal buyer. GCCs are consolidating into fewer, larger campuses (Bangalore, Hyderabad, Pune) and exiting secondary markets. This explains why office absorption is collapsing while retail (consumer-facing, experiential) is thriving. Implication: (1) Sell office REITs; they are exposed to legacy IT services demand that is structurally declining. (2) Overweight retail REITs and malls — consumer spending is robust (GST +14.8% YoY, PV sales +16% YoY, 2W sales +19.7% YoY). (3) Nifty IT's flat performance is justified — the sector is losing real estate optionality. (4) Expect office rents to compress 10-15% in secondary markets (Delhi, Mumbai) over next 12 months as supply exceeds GCC demand.","pct_10y":6,"pct_note":"Office absorption at 6th percentile is a structural break, not cyclical. Retail vacancy at 7th percentile (tightest in 10 years) shows capital is rotating from office to consumer-facing real estate. This divergence has not been priced into REIT valuations.","is_surprise":true}

{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

Capex Cycle Accelerates Into a Narrowing Credit Channel

The facts:

  • IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY and capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (up from 75.6%) confirm the investment cycle is broadening, not just budgeted.
  • But bank credit at 17.1% YoY vs deposit growth at 10.8% YoY — a 630bps gap — means the funding base for that capex is thinning.
  • PMI composite at 54.6 (83rd percentile) flatters: manufacturing PMI fell to 52.8 while services carried the headline.
  • Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile, 10-year high) is feeding WPI at 9.92% YoY — a pipeline that reaches core CPI with a two-quarter lag.
  • But two-wheeler sales at 19.7% YoY outpacing PV at 16% YoY signals rural demand is holding — the informal economy is not yet cracking.

The tension: The capex cycle is real — capacity utilisation and IIP capital goods confirm it — but the credit channel financing it is under structural stress. A cycle that cannot fund itself through deposits or bond markets eventually stalls.

Bottom line: Watch corporate bond issuance: a sustained print below ₹20,000 cr / month signals the credit channel is closing faster than the capex pipeline can absorb.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

DM Equities at Peak Valuations — Bond Market Disagrees

The facts:

  • Euro Stoxx 50 at 6,173 (100th percentile) and S&P 500 at 7,812 (100th percentile) are pricing a growth re-acceleration that nominal GDP data does not support.
  • US 10Y Treasury at 5.22% yield (95th percentile) — even after slipping from 5.28% — is doing the tightening the Fed has paused on; US GDP SAAR recovered to 2.2% SAAR but from a 1.5% trough.
  • But US core CPI at 2.45% YoY is falling for two consecutive months — the Fed's disinflation case is intact, which is why equities are holding.
  • BOJ at 1.0% p.a. (86th percentile, up from 0.75%) is the underappreciated tail: yen carry unwind accelerates as the rate differential compresses.
  • China GDP at 4.3% YoY (down from 5.0%) with PMI composite at 49.5 (contraction) removes the commodity reflation backstop.

The tension: DM equity markets are pricing a soft landing; DM bond markets are pricing persistent tightening. China's deceleration means commodity prices cannot sustain the reflation narrative that would justify current equity multiples.

Bottom line: BOJ rate trajectory is the single most important variable for EM carry flows — watch the next BOJ meeting for a signal above 1.25% p.a.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

Domestic Liquidity Robust — Structural Deposit Gap Underneath

The facts:

  • SIP inflows at ₹32,297 cr / month (92nd percentile, rising two consecutive months) and DII equity net at ₹58,502 cr net / month (100th percentile) are providing a structural bid to Indian equities.
  • FII equity net turned sharply positive at ₹29,631 cr net / month (83rd percentile) — reversing from -₹3,112 cr net / month prior — but the sequence shows volatility, not conviction.
  • But deposit growth at 10.8% YoY against credit at 17.1% YoY means the banking system is funding credit expansion by drawing down liquidity buffers, not growing the deposit base.
  • Corporate bond issuance at ₹18,700 cr / month (0th percentile — lowest decile in a decade) confirms capital markets are not recycling savings into credit efficiently.

The tension: Surface liquidity — SIPs, DII flows, FII reversal — looks abundant. Structural liquidity — the deposit base that funds bank credit — is being depleted. These two can coexist until they cannot: the trigger is typically a macro-prudential circular on risk weights.

Bottom line: FII equity net is the swing variable: a reversal back below zero — given INR at 97.09 and US 10Y at 5.22% yield — would expose how thin the structural liquidity cushion is.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

NRI Demand and Luxury Supply Diverge From Office REIT Reality

The facts:

  • NRI buying is RISING — NRI share of residential purchases at 20% (up 5 percentage points), with NRI share within premium/luxury at 25%; remittances at $140 bn (12.8% YoY) are the funding source.
  • Hyderabad leads city momentum: residential sales +15% YoY with launches +120% YoY — a supply surge that 29 months of unsold inventory will test; Bengaluru at +12% YoY sales with prices up 8% YoY is the more disciplined market.
  • Office absorption at 13.2 mn sq ft / quarter (6th percentile, 10-year low) contradicts the leasing narrative: GCCs at 41% of occupier mix are absorbing space, but IT services at 15% are retrenching.
  • REIT valuations reflect the office stress: Embassy at ₹370/unit (down 14% from ₹431) and Mindspace at ₹345/unit (down 30% from ₹491) are pricing a structural demand shift, not a cyclical dip.
  • Bank Nifty at 55,257 (91st percentile) is pricing credit growth, not CD ratio stress — a derating risk if the RBI moves on risk weights.

The tension: Residential real estate — especially premium and luxury, NRI-driven — is holding on remittance flows and aspirational demand. Office real estate is repricing a structural GCC-vs-IT-services shift that REIT unit prices are only beginning to reflect.

Bottom line: Avoid office REITs until absorption recovers above 16 mn sq ft / quarter; overweight residential developers with Hyderabad and Bengaluru exposure where NRI demand provides a floor.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Four Fault Lines, One Trigger Point

The facts:

  • Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile) feeding into WPI at 9.92% YoY — if Brent holds above $100/bbl, core CPI breaches 4.5% YoY within two quarters, forcing RBI off its pause.
  • CD ratio at 81.4% credit ÷ deposits with corporate bond issuance at a decade low: NBFC funding stress is the most probable near-term credit event, probability high, impact systemic.
  • INR at 97.09 (94th percentile, depreciating 4 of last 5 months) — a sustained move above 98 triggers RBI FX intervention that draws down reserves and tightens domestic liquidity simultaneously.
  • BOJ at 1.0% p.a. (86th percentile): any signal of acceleration toward 1.5% p.a. unwinds yen carry trades, pressures EM currencies including INR, and reverses FII equity flows that just turned positive.

The tension: Each risk is individually manageable; the danger is sequencing — fuel inflation forces RBI hawkishness precisely as BOJ tightening pressures INR, which tightens domestic liquidity at the moment the CD ratio has least room to absorb it.

Bottom line: Watch RBI's next inflation commentary: an upward revision above 5.5% YoY in the forecast signals the pause is over and the rate cycle has turned.

"}
